---
title: Develop locally with listen
description: Receive your app's webhook events on a laptop the ClipMux server can't reach, signed so your handler verifies them unchanged.
---

While you develop, your app runs on `localhost`, and the ClipMux server
can't POST webhooks to it. `listen` fixes that without a tunnel: it
long-polls your app's events from the server and forwards each one to your
local handler, signed as a real delivery would be. Your handler's code
doesn't change between development and production.

There are two versions: `npx @clipmux/node listen` for apps built with the
Node SDK, and the server binary's `clipmux listen` for any other language.

## Before you start

- `CLIPMUX_URL` and `CLIPMUX_API_KEY` for your app, in your env file or
  environment. The key needs `assets:read`, which the default scopes
  include.
- Your app running locally, with its webhook handler.
- Your app doesn't need a webhook endpoint registered for this. `listen`
  reads the same events an endpoint would receive.

## With @clipmux/node [#with-clipmuxnode]

```bash
npx @clipmux/node listen --forward-to localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook
```

```txt
Forwarding "My app dev" events to http://localhost:3000/api/clipmux/webhook, signed with CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Ctrl-C stops.
✓ video.asset.ready ast_… → 200
```

It signs each event with your own `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, so
`clipmuxHandler` or `clipmux.webhooks.verify` accepts it as it is. Any
secret works here. If your app has no webhook endpoint yet, `init` writes a
local one (`whsec_local_…`) for `listen`, and `doctor` warns that it's for
`listen` only.

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--forward-to URL` | Your local webhook URL. Required. Without a scheme, `http://` is assumed. |
| `--since DURATION` | Also replay events from this long ago, such as `10m` or `2h`. Without it, only new events. |
| `--events LIST` | Only these event types, comma separated, such as `video.asset.ready,video.asset.track.ready`. |
| `--env-file FILE` | Where to read the settings. Default `.env.local`, or `.env` if there's no `.env.local`. |

Each event is tried up to four times if your handler is unreachable or
answers `5xx`, then `listen` moves on.

## With clipmux listen, for any language

The server binary has its own `listen`. It signs with a secret it makes
for you, which you set as your app's webhook secret:

```bash
CLIPMUX_API_KEY=cmx_… clipmux listen --server https://video.example.com --forward-to localhost:8000/webhooks
```

```txt
Forwarding events to http://localhost:8000/webhooks
Webhook secret: whsec_…  (set it as your app's webhook secret; it stays the same next time)
```

It reads `CLIPMUX_API_KEY` from the environment, not from an env file. The
secret is kept in a `clipmux` folder in your user's config directory (or
`CLIPMUX_AGENT_DIR`), so it stays the same between runs. To choose it yourself, set `CLIPMUX_LISTEN_SECRET`. `--server`
defaults to `CLIPMUX_SERVER`, then `CLIPMUX_URL`. It takes `--events` and
`--since` like the Node version; `--since` takes a Go duration such as
`10m` or `1h30m`. See [Command line](/docs/reference/cli).

## What it forwards

Each event is POSTed to your URL exactly as a webhook endpoint receives it,
with the same headers: `X-Webhook-Event`, `X-Webhook-Id`,
`X-Webhook-Timestamp` and `X-Webhook-Signature`. Underneath, both versions
read `GET /v1/events`, the app's events oldest first, long-polling for new
ones.

`listen` sees only your API key's app. Make a separate ClipMux app for each
developer, so your test uploads and events don't mix with anyone else's or
with production.

## Check it works

1. Start your app, then `listen`.
2. Upload a short file to the same app:

   ```bash
   npx @clipmux/node upload sample.mp4 --passthrough lesson_42
   ```

3. When encoding finishes, `listen` prints `✓ video.asset.ready ast_… → 200`.

If the line shows another status, it's your handler's answer:

- `400`: the signature didn't verify. With `npx @clipmux/node listen`, your
  app must read the same `CLIPMUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. With `clipmux listen`,
  set your app's secret to the one it printed.
- `404`: `--forward-to` isn't your handler's route.
- `unreachable`: nothing is listening on that port.
